You have access to comprehensive Todoist management tools for personal productivity and team collaboration. Use these tools to help users manage tasks, projects, sections, comments, and assignments effectively.

23	**Salt is the preferred method for system administration.** A change that can be

# Infrastructure preferences — Rick Ashford

Read by any skill that provisions, containerises, scripts, or deploys.

Companion files: `lab.md` (ash4d lab conventions and repo rules), `working.md`
(how to interact and what counts as verified).

## Containers

- **Images we author default to SUSE / openSUSE BCI base images.** Any
  deviation needs a stated justification and my authorisation before
  proceeding. Example of the rule applied correctly: `dli-power-mcp` builds on
  `registry.suse.com/bci/python`.
- **Pulling a maintained upstream image is not a deviation.** cloudflared,
  nut_exporter and similar vendor-maintained images get used directly — no
  flag, no authorisation request. The policy exists to keep our own build
  artifacts on a supported base, so wrapping someone else's binary in a BCI
  image to satisfy the letter of the rule buys nothing and creates a build path
  to own.

## Configuration management

**Salt is the preferred method for system administration.** A change that can be
expressed as a salt state should be, rather than a one-off SSH command or a
shell script copied to each host. Master is `pecan`; states and pillar live in
the `ash4d-salt` repo.

- **Salt owns the hosts.** Packages, files, services, users, OS-level config.
- **Fleet and `kubectl` own cluster workloads.** Salt manages the machine k3s
  runs on; Fleet manages what runs inside k3s. Keep that line — a salt state
  that applies a manifest puts two systems in charge of the same object.
- Prefer `state.apply` over `cmd.run`. `cmd.run` is permitted and deliberate —
  arbitrary execution at my request is the point of the open eauth ACL — but a
  change worth making twice belongs in a state file.
- Run `state.apply test=True` and show me the diff before applying. `state_verbose`
  is off, so a converged host prints nothing; output means drift, and the diff
  is the interesting part.
- Long operations go through the async API and poll the job. A synchronous call
  blocks until every minion returns and will time out on a real highstate.
- Every job is recorded in the master job cache with user, target, function and
  arguments. That record is the audit trail. Do not SSH to a host to do
  something salt could have done — it bypasses the record.
- Minion layout is not uniform. Package names, config paths and service names
  differ between stock `salt-minion` and the Uyuni Salt Bundle; branch on the
  `saltpath` grain rather than `os_family`. Which host runs which is state —
  it lives in Claude memory, not here.

## Languages

- **Python and Bash** for tooling, automation, harnesses and pipelines.
- Assume competence in Linux and Kubernetes; skip the primer and give me the
  command.

## Git

### Writing into a repo

- **Never Write or Edit into a repo containing `.entire/` from a Cowork
  session.** This covers new files, not only edits, and applies whether or not
  a commit follows. Check before *writing* — checking at commit time is the
  wrong gate and has already let bad writes through.
- Why: entire.io captures agent work through hooks
  (`.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`). Cowork
  does not run those hooks, so anything Cowork writes into the repo lands with
  no checkpoint lineage and the repo's provenance breaks silently.
- Instead: stage the artifacts to the session scratch dir or the mounted
  `_portfolio` folder, then hand me the file list and intended destination
  paths so I can run it through Claude Code in one step. If something genuinely
  must land immediately — a live incident — say so and get explicit
  authorisation first.
- Applying manifests to a cluster with `kubectl` is fine. It is repo *files*
  that are gated.
- Known entire-tracked repos are listed in `lab.md`.

### Committing

- Before any commit, verify `.entire/settings.json` exists and is correct. If
  it is missing, stop and tell me — do not commit. Never claim entire.io is
  enabled; it can only be verified, not enabled by you.
- Repositories that sync to **darthzen**: leave `.entire/settings.json` and the
  agent hook files committed, and let `entire/checkpoints/v1` push normally.
- Repositories that sync anywhere else: before the first commit, verify entire
  is configured with either `--skip-push-sessions` or
  `--checkpoint-remote github:darthzen/<repo>-checkpoints`. The
  `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch must never reach a remote I do not own. Do not
  stage `.entire/` or agent hook files into a pull request against that repo —
  use `entire enable --local` so the config stays in `settings.local.json`,
  which is gitignored.
- Commit only on my explicit instruction. I handle git.

## Secrets

- Credentials live in `~/Developer/keys/<service>/`, never in a doc, a
  preferences file, or a repo.
- Do not copy a token, key, or PAT into any file you create, including files in
  this folder. Reference where it lives instead.

## Working in a sandbox

- A sandboxed shell may be able to create files under `.git/` but not delete
  them, which strands `index.lock` and blocks every later git command. If a
  delete fails with "Operation not permitted", request delete permission for
  the folder rather than leaving the lock in place.
- Cloud-synced folders (iCloud, Dropbox) may hold files that exist only in the
  cloud. A shell command will error on those; reading the file downloads it
  first.
- The sandboxed shell and the file tools do not share a filesystem. Paths under
  the Claude application-support tree — memory files among them — are reachable
  by the file tools only.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build ZoiaCanvas Release and package it as a drag-to-install DMG:
# app icon on the left, an /Applications symlink on the right.
#
# Usage: tools/make_dmg.sh
#
# Signing: if a "Developer ID Application" identity is in the keychain,
# the app is re-signed with it (hardened runtime + audio-input
# entitlement) so the DMG passes Gatekeeper on other Macs. Otherwise the
# development signature from the build is kept and the script warns —
# fine for your own machines, blocked on everyone else's.
#
# Notarization: set NOTARY_PROFILE to a `notarytool store-credentials`
# profile name to notarize and staple after signing. Skipped otherwise.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
APP_NAME="ZoiaCanvas"
DIST="$REPO/dist"
BUILD="$(mktemp -d /tmp/zoiacanvas-build.XXXXXX)"
STAGE="$(mktemp -d /tmp/zoiacanvas-dmg.XXXXXX)"
trap 'rm -rf "$BUILD" "$STAGE"' EXIT

cd "$REPO"
[ -d "$APP_NAME.xcodeproj" ] || xcodegen generate

echo "==> Building Release"
xcodebuild -project "$APP_NAME.xcodeproj" -scheme "$APP_NAME" \
    -configuration Release -derivedDataPath "$BUILD" \
    build | tail -3

APP="$BUILD/Build/Products/Release/$APP_NAME.app"
[ -d "$APP" ] || { echo "error: $APP not found" >&2; exit 1; }

VERSION="$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print CFBundleShortVersionString' \
    "$APP/Contents/Info.plist")"

DEV_ID="$(security find-identity -v -p codesigning \
    | awk -F'"' '/Developer ID Application/ {print $2; exit}')"

if [ -n "$DEV_ID" ]; then
    echo "==> Signing with: $DEV_ID (hardened runtime)"
    codesign --force --sign "$DEV_ID" --options runtime --timestamp \
        --entitlements "$REPO/tools/$APP_NAME.entitlements" "$APP"
    codesign --verify --strict --deep "$APP"
else
    echo "warning: no Developer ID Application identity in keychain." >&2
    echo "warning: keeping the development signature — Gatekeeper will" >&2
    echo "warning: block this app on other people's Macs." >&2
fi

if [ -n "${NOTARY_PROFILE:-}" ]; then
    if [ -z "$DEV_ID" ]; then
        echo "error: NOTARY_PROFILE set but no Developer ID identity;" \
             "notarization requires a Developer ID signature" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "==> Notarizing (profile: $NOTARY_PROFILE)"
    ditto -c -k --keepParent "$APP" "$BUILD/$APP_NAME.zip"
    xcrun notarytool submit "$BUILD/$APP_NAME.zip" \
        --keychain-profile "$NOTARY_PROFILE" --wait
    xcrun stapler staple "$APP"
fi

echo "==> Staging DMG contents"
cp -R "$APP" "$STAGE/"
ln -s /Applications "$STAGE/Applications"

DMG="$DIST/$APP_NAME-$VERSION.dmg"
RW_DMG="$BUILD/rw.dmg"
mkdir -p "$DIST"
rm -f "$DMG"

echo "==> Creating DMG"
hdiutil create -srcfolder "$STAGE" -volname "$APP_NAME" \
    -fs HFS+ -format UDRW -ov "$RW_DMG" >/dev/null

MOUNT="/Volumes/$APP_NAME"
hdiutil attach "$RW_DMG" -mountpoint "$MOUNT" -nobrowse >/dev/null

# Finder window layout: icon view, app left, Applications right.
osascript <<EOF
tell application "Finder"
    tell disk "$APP_NAME"
        open
        set current view of container window to icon view
        set toolbar visible of container window to false
        set statusbar visible of container window to false
        set the bounds of container window to {200, 200, 760, 560}
        set opts to the icon view options of container window
        set arrangement of opts to not arranged
        set icon size of opts to 112
        set position of item "$APP_NAME.app" of container window to {150, 160}
        set position of item "Applications" of container window to {410, 160}
        close
        open
        update without registering applications
        delay 1
        close
    end tell
end tell
EOF
sync
hdiutil detach "$MOUNT" >/dev/null

hdiutil convert "$RW_DMG" -format UDZO -imagekey zlib-level=9 \
    -ov -o "$DMG" >/dev/null

if [ -n "$DEV_ID" ]; then
    codesign --force --sign "$DEV_ID" --timestamp "$DMG"
fi

echo "==> $DMG"

# app icon on the left, an /Applications symlink on the right.
#
# Usage: tools/make_dmg.sh
#
# Signing: if a "Developer ID Application" identity is in the keychain,
# the app is re-signed with it (hardened runtime + audio-input
# entitlement) so the DMG passes Gatekeeper on other Macs. Otherwise the
# development signature from the build is kept and the script warns —
# fine for your own machines, blocked on everyone else's.
#
# Notarization: set NOTARY_PROFILE to a `notarytool store-credentials`
# profile name to notarize and staple after signing. Skipped otherwise.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
APP_NAME="ZoiaCanvas"
DIST="$REPO/dist"
BUILD="$(mktemp -d /tmp/zoiacanvas-build.XXXXXX)"
STAGE="$(mktemp -d /tmp/zoiacanvas-dmg.XXXXXX)"
trap 'rm -rf "$BUILD" "$STAGE"' EXIT

cd "$REPO"
[ -d "$APP_NAME.xcodeproj" ] || xcodegen generate

echo "==> Building Release"
xcodebuild -project "$APP_NAME.xcodeproj" -scheme "$APP_NAME" \
    -configuration Release -derivedDataPath "$BUILD" \
    build | tail -3

APP="$BUILD/Build/Products/Release/$APP_NAME.app"
[ -d "$APP" ] || { echo "error: $APP not found" >&2; exit 1; }

VERSION="$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print CFBundleShortVersionString' \
    "$APP/Contents/Info.plist")"

DEV_ID="$(security find-identity -v -p codesigning \
    | awk -F'"' '/Developer ID Application/ {print $2; exit}')"

if [ -n "$DEV_ID" ]; then
    echo "==> Signing with: $DEV_ID (hardened runtime)"
    codesign --force --sign "$DEV_ID" --options runtime --timestamp \
        --entitlements "$REPO/tools/$APP_NAME.entitlements" "$APP"
    codesign --verify --strict --deep "$APP"
else
    echo "warning: no Developer ID Application identity in keychain." >&2
    echo "warning: keeping the development signature — Gatekeeper will" >&2
    echo "warning: block this app on other people's Macs." >&2
fi

if [ -n "${NOTARY_PROFILE:-}" ]; then
    if [ -z "$DEV_ID" ]; then
        echo "error: NOTARY_PROFILE set but no Developer ID identity;" \
             "notarization requires a Developer ID signature" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "==> Notarizing (profile: $NOTARY_PROFILE)"
    ditto -c -k --keepParent "$APP" "$BUILD/$APP_NAME.zip"
    xcrun notarytool submit "$BUILD/$APP_NAME.zip" \
        --keychain-profile "$NOTARY_PROFILE" --wait
    xcrun stapler staple "$APP"
fi

echo "==> Staging DMG contents"
cp -R "$APP" "$STAGE/"
ln -s /Applications "$STAGE/Applications"

DMG="$DIST/$APP_NAME-$VERSION.dmg"
RW_DMG="$BUILD/rw.dmg"
mkdir -p "$DIST"
rm -f "$DMG"

echo "==> Creating DMG"
hdiutil create -srcfolder "$STAGE" -volname "$APP_NAME" \
    -fs HFS+ -format UDRW -ov "$RW_DMG" >/dev/null

MOUNT="/Volumes/$APP_NAME"
hdiutil attach "$RW_DMG" -mountpoint "$MOUNT" -nobrowse >/dev/null

# Finder window layout: icon view, app left, Applications right.
osascript <<EOF
tell application "Finder"
    tell disk "$APP_NAME"
        open
        set current view of container window to icon view
        set toolbar visible of container window to false
        set statusbar visible of container window to false
        set the bounds of container window to {200, 200, 760, 560}
        set opts to the icon view options of container window
        set arrangement of opts to not arranged
        set icon size of opts to 112
        set position of item "$APP_NAME.app" of container window to {150, 160}
        set position of item "Applications" of container window to {410, 160}
        close
        open
        update without registering applications
        delay 1
        close
    end tell
end tell
EOF
sync
hdiutil detach "$MOUNT" >/dev/null

hdiutil convert "$RW_DMG" -format UDZO -imagekey zlib-level=9 \
    -ov -o "$DMG" >/dev/null

if [ -n "$DEV_ID" ]; then
    codesign --force --sign "$DEV_ID" --timestamp "$DMG"
fi

echo "==> $DMG"

All four items are done. Summary:

**Signing answer:** "Mac Developer" is the right identity for building and running on your own machines — it resolves to your "Apple Development: Rick Ashford" certificate. It is the wrong one for a DMG other people download: Gatekeeper blocks development-signed apps on any Mac not registered to your team, and macOS 15+ removed the right-click-Open bypass. Distribution outside the App Store needs a **Developer ID Application** certificate plus notarization. Your keychain doesn't have one yet, so I put a 30-minute block on your calendar tomorrow at 9:45 (after the salt-api fix) with the exact steps — cert creation in Xcode, `notarytool store-credentials`, and the rebuild command. Until then the DMG works on your Macs only.

**Bundle ID:** The root cause was `project.yml` — the project is xcodegen-generated, so your pbxproj correction would have been wiped on the next `xcodegen generate`. I changed `bundleIdPrefix` to `ash4d` and moved your team (`5YR793D4UZ`) and Mac Developer identity into `project.yml`, regenerated, and verified the pbxproj now comes out with `ash4d.ZoiaCanvas` for both app and tests.

**Icon:** It was implemented (commit fe7f7fb), but rendered as pastel LEDs on a light grey tile — that's the generic look you saw. Rebuilt it: black tile, same 8×5 module-run layout, ZOIA header colors at full saturation with glow. Preview sent above; the new `.icns` replaced the old one in `Sources/ZoiaCanvas/Resources/` and I confirmed by checksum it's the one inside the built app.

**DMG:** `tools/make_dmg.sh` builds Release, signs, stages the app with an `/Applications` symlink, and sets the Finder layout — app on the left, Applications link on the right, drag to install. Ran it end-to-end: `dist/ZoiaCanvas-1.0.0.dmg` built, mounted, and verified (symlink present, layout saved, signature `ash4d.ZoiaCanvas` / team `5YR793D4UZ`). Once the Developer ID cert exists, the same script picks it up automatically, signs with hardened runtime plus the audio-input entitlement (`tools/ZoiaCanvas.entitlements` — required so the mic keeps working under hardened runtime), and notarizes when `NOTARY_PROFILE` is set.

Changed files, uncommitted — git is yours: `project.yml`, `.gitignore` (added `dist/`), `Sources/ZoiaCanvas/Resources/ZoiaCanvas.icns`, `tools/make_dmg.sh`, `tools/ZoiaCanvas.entitlements`.

ZoiaCanvas-1.0.0.zip
---BODY---
First public release.

Design Empress Effects ZOIA patches on a Mac: a node canvas over real `.bin` patch files, with live audio playback and signal animation.

## Highlights

- **Node canvas** — modules as nodes, cables you can see, pages as side-by-side bands with LED-grid previews
- **Live playback** — hear the patch; wires draw the audio they carry, gates pulse down CV cables, modules glow with their output
- **Full editing** — searchable palette, drag wiring (pick a cable up off a port to re-route it), every option and param in the inspector
- **Pedal-true grid placement** — drag modules onto the 8×5 button grid the pedal will show; placement is sticky
- **A window per patch** — compare patches side by side; the whole workspace, window frames, and every patch's canvas arrangement come back on relaunch
- **Byte-verified format** — encoder and decoder round-trip the entire ZOIA and Euroburo factory libraries; what you save is what the pedal reads

## Download note

`ZoiaCanvas-1.0.0.zip` is not notarized (no Developer ID yet): macOS will warn on first launch. Right-click → Open, or approve it under System Settings → Privacy & Security. Building from source (`xcodegen && xcodebuild -scheme ZoiaCanvas build`) avoids the warning entirely.

Requires macOS 15+. Audio engine covers a growing subset of the module catalog; unimplemented modules pass silence, and pitch/LFO curves are documented approximations pending hardware calibration.
